resources.title: AO Guide — full free astronomy-olympiad textbook
resources.why: "The guide goes over pretty much all of the theoretical concepts needed for astronomy olympiads." Prerequisites: "basic understanding of high school level mathematics and physics. Familiarity with calculus and basic mechanics is required." Units: Positional Astronomy (The Sphere · Coordinate Systems · Time · Perturbation in Astronomical Observations · Sun, Moon and Planets) · Photometry (Radiometry · Magnitude Systems · Radiation Mechanism · Detectors · Types of Telescopes) · Celestial Mechanics (Kepler's Laws · Bound Orbits · Unbound Orbits · Orbital Elements · Three Body Systems · Orbital Maneuvers · General Relativity) · Stellar Astrophysics (Stellar Structure · Classification · Binary Systems · Stellar Evolution · Solar System) · Galactic Astrophysics (Galaxies · The Milky Way) · Cosmology (Our Universe · Geometry of the Universe · The Friedmann Equations) · Practical Astronomy. Each unit has an "Advanced Topics" section and a Recommended Reading list.

gaps.missing: ⭐⭐ No Nepali data-analysis training material — despite Data Analysis being 150 of the IOAA's 600 marks (25 %), more than Telescope + Sky Map + Planetarium combined. NASO's own Stage-3 description reduces it to *"mean, median, regression, and error estimation."* The official IOAA Syllabus A.3 demands far more: error-source identification, error calculation and influence estimation, polar and logarithmic graph papers, linearisation and best-fit lines, and basic statistical analysis of observational data.
gaps.evidence: Verified IOAA 2025 mark scheme (300 theory / 150 data analysis / 50 / 50 / 50) against NASO's Stage-3 description and IOAA Syllabus A.3.
gaps.aiSpec: Generate "Data Analysis for NAO & IOAA — a Nepal Manual" in 5 parts, each with a worked astronomical dataset: (1) Error treatment — error sources, absolute/relative/percentage error, propagation through addition/subtraction/multiplication/division/powers, standard deviation, standard error of the mean, reporting a result ± uncertainty with correct significant figures (IOAA A.1 clause 6 explicitly requires this). (2) Graphing — choosing scales, linear / log-linear / log-log / polar paper, converting a power law y = axᵇ into a straight line by taking logs, best-fit by eye vs least squares, gradient and intercept with uncertainties, residual plots. (3) The six canonical astronomy plots — Hubble diagram (v vs d → H₀), Cepheid period–luminosity (log P vs M → distance modulus), HR diagram (colour index vs absolute magnitude), light curves of eclipsing binaries (→ radii, inclination), radial-velocity curves (→ mass function), 21 cm line profiles (→ rotation curves, dark matter). Each with real open data (NASA Exoplanet Archive, Gaia, SIMBAD) and a full worked solution. (4) Statistics — mean, median, mode, variance, χ² goodness-of-fit for a model light curve, t-test for comparing two samples, weighted means for repeated measurements. (5) The IOAA answer-sheet discipline — how marks are allocated on the official Summary Answersheets (all four are free in the IOAA 2025 set), units, significant digits, and how to earn partial credit. Anchor everything to the freely available IOAA 2025 Data Analysis Questions + Solutions and the 2016–2019 DA solutions. Also point students to Ayush Tiwari's Practical Handouts (S14), written by a Nepali IOAA 2025 team member, which already covers much of this.

gaps.missing: ⭐ No Nepali observational-astronomy training. Half the IOAA is practical, and its Observation component has three distinct sub-rounds — Telescope, Sky Map, Planetarium — each worth 50 marks and each requiring a different skill. Nepal has no telescope access programme, and NASO's own Stage-3 description concedes the observational exam is *"often paper-based."* Nepal has never won an IOAA medal (3 HMs, 0 medals), and the Observation rounds are the most likely explanation.
gaps.evidence: Verified: IOAA 2025 published separate Question/Solution/Instructions/Summary-Answersheet sets for Telescope, Sky Map and Planetarium; NASO's Stage-3 text says *"observational astronomy (often paper-based)"*; IOAA Syllabus A.3 requires *"usage of basic astronomical instruments — telescopes and various detectors"*, *"naked-eye observations"*, *"sky maps and catalogues"*, *"magnitude estimation, estimation of angular separation."*
gaps.aiSpec: Generate "Observational Astronomy for Nepal — a no-telescope training programme": (a) Sky Map round — a 30-session naked-eye curriculum using Stellarium set to Kathmandu 27.7° N plus Stellar Guesser and Skychart Tasks; constellation-by-constellation identification drills; magnitude estimation by comparison against known stars; angular separation by hand measurement; the A3 star maps from IOAA 2025 (Map-OM01/OM02/OP01/OP02/OT01, all free with solutions) as the practice bank. (b) Planetarium round — since Nepal has no planetarium, build a virtual planetarium protocol using Stellarium's planetarium-mode projection plus the free IOAA 2025 Observation-Planetarium Questions and Solutions; drill the four standard task types (identify the object, give coordinates, predict rising/setting time, interpret a simulated view). (c) Telescope round — a low-cost hardware programme: specify a ₹/Rs-budget build (a 60 mm refractor or a Dobsonian from local materials), plus paper-and-simulation substitutes — the IOAA Telescope round is largely about *reading* an instrument and *interpreting* an eyepiece view, which can be trained entirely from the free IOAA 2025 Telescope Questions/Solutions plus Stellarium's eyepiece-view simulator. (d) A "Nepal Dark-Sky Sessions" calendar — new-moon dates, Kathmandu-valley light-pollution advice, and 6 accessible dark sites by province. (e) Ask NASO for one shared telescope per province — 7 instruments would cover all 7 provincial centres; cost this proposal and hand it to NASO.
